set.body:
Why (highest leverage): PairedDualityDiagram holds two diagrams + a shared sample space, but the paired estimators ignore it and compute the unweighted cross-covariance X'Y/(n-1) (Decompositions.scala:61-62,122-131,211-215). Two-table methods are the SVD of the shared-row-metric cross-operator Q_X^{1/2} X'D Y Q_Y^{1/2}: PLSC=(I,I); CCA=(Sxx^-1,Syy^-1) with ridge = Q shrunk toward I; RRR = asymmetric (metric on one side; direction = which side gets identity).

Scope: add DualityKernels.crossGram(paired, policy) computing the metric-weighted cross-operator with the same storage discipline as rowGram/colGram; re-express Plsc/Cca/ReducedRankRegression as one PairedGmd routine parameterized by (Q_X,Q_Y). Regularization becomes a metric; direction becomes a metric choice. NOTE: the win is cohesion + free D-weighting + deleting three bespoke paths — NOT performance (CCA still forms and inverts the column Gram).

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] crossGram added with storage-policy handling and tests (dense, diagonal-metric, sparse) mirroring DualityKernelsSuite.
- [ ] Plsc/Cca/RRR share one PairedGmd routine; the three bespoke cross-product paths are deleted.
- [ ] A non-identity row metric D produces D-weighted PLSC/CCA (new capability), covered by a test.
- [ ] Ridge regularization is expressed as a Q (metric), not a code branch.
- [ ] Paired parity fixtures pass unchanged — identical values to pre-refactor for the identity-D case — on JVM+JS.
Blocked by the parity-fixtures item; sequence after the unified-LatentFit and projection-contract items.
set.title: multivar: KEYSTONE — crossGram; express PLSC/CCA/RRR as one PairedGmd under (Q_X,Q_Y)
